chapter: Club Alabam and the Europe contract
title: Will Marion Cook teaches him to retard for a singer
summary: He asks Will Marion Cook how to slow down with Abbie Mitchell and learns to bend his knees on each retard.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: No, it was the Club Alabam's show. Just like The Cotton Club's show, it was called the Club Alabam's show. But this was a great show. And I learnt one thing, because Abby Mitchell was a great star in those days, you see. She could sing very well. Will Marion Cook used to come there because that was his wife and set down there. And a lot of others used to come there during the rehearsal days. And I could then pick up the tempo, but I didn't know how to retard the tempo along with the singer. So I just wasn't afraid to go over to Old Man Cook, and I said, "Listen Daddy Cook, Daddy," I said, "how do you retard a singer?" Because she was singing a song called "Red, Red Rose", and there was a part where you had to retard it. And when you retard and stay with the singer too. And he said, "Son, just bend your legs with each retard." And I didn't realize that, you just go and you bend your knees, bend your knees as you go down, you can retard right with the singer and get in rhythm with her voice, you know? And after that -- because I didn't know how to retard. I knew how to pick up, anybody can pick up something. But retard it, and stay in rhythm, you know what I mean, and at the same time slow down. So, that's one thing I learned. The next thing, I learned a very good thing, too. To do for any musician who may be happening to be listening to this
